# website-rebuild-skill

## Differences from Upstream

This package is a fork of [boyang-hu/website-rebuild-skill](https://github.com/boyang-hu/website-rebuild-skill), merged up to and including upstream v0.1.73. It records only what differs from upstream; for what the skill is and how to run it, read `skills/website-rebuild/SKILL.md`.

### Engineering additions

Capability this fork adds for real deployment environments (WSL2, Docker, Linux root, cross-platform Chrome) and for framework-driven SPAs:

- consolidates cross-platform Chrome/Chromium binary discovery into `scripts/lib/chrome.mjs` (`findChrome`), eliminating duplicate and inconsistent candidate lists across `probe.mjs`, `netcapture.mjs`, and `pixelcompare.mjs` while adding Windows and Linux default executable fallbacks;
- adds automatic `--no-sandbox` flag injection for headless Chrome when running in Linux root environments (such as WSL2 and Docker containers) to prevent browser startup crashes;
- introduces `CHROME_FLAGS` environment variable support in `scripts/lib/chrome.mjs` for passing custom runtime flags to headless Chrome instances;
- isolates CDP targets per route in `scripts/netcapture.mjs` (`Target.createTarget` / `Target.closeTarget`) to prevent WebGL context and DOM memory leaks across SPA multi-route crawls;
- makes an unrecognised `--viewports` key FATAL in `scripts/netcapture.mjs`. The selection was a filter with no floor under it, so a typo (`mobil`), the wrong case (`Mobile`) or a space after the comma left an EMPTY set — the capture loop ran zero times and the run still printed `requests observed: 0 / MIRROR GAPS: 0` over a header-only ledger. ⚠ **GAP=0 is the number the caller came for, and here it was computed over nothing observed.** Keys are trimmed, and a partial typo (`desktop,mobil`) is fatal too rather than capturing half the matrix and reporting it as the whole;
- gives the closure gate in `scripts/verify-mirror.mjs` the off-host census it was missing. The gate's host set is DERIVED from the ledger, so every reference to a host the crawler never fetched from was dropped inside the extractor in silence while `reference set − disk set = ∅` printed green over a set the gate had itself narrowed. Counted per host now, and loud when the host names a file and `external.txt` carries no whole-host decision for it. ⭐ The ranking and the "is this an asset host?" judgement live in `lib/extract-refs.mjs` (`createOffHostCensus`) and are **shared with `mirror-site.mjs`** rather than copied — the blind spot that module's own header warns about — and the census keys on ANY asset-shaped reference rather than the first one seen, because a library CDN is routinely named by its extension-less base before any of its files;
- expands `scripts/module-map.mjs` with Webpack 4/5 JSONP chunk container parsing (`/(?:webpackJsonp|webpackChunk)/i`), ESM export helpers (`__webpack_require__.d`), and second-parameter CommonJS export extraction. Container selection is a **priority chain** — JSONP, then the TURBOPACK push, then the generic `key: function` scan, then the array form — because a positive structural signature beats a count: a Turbopack chunk can carry more webpack-shaped properties inside its module bodies than it has modules. ⚠ This subsumes upstream v0.1.69's `turbo.length >= 1` tiebreak, which is therefore **not carried**: left in, its unconditional arm would replace a correctly identified JSONP container whenever a TURBOPACK push is also present;
- splits the two jobs `KNOWN.has(id)` was doing in `scripts/module-map.mjs`'s require scan. **Shape** decides whether a literal is a module id at all — without it, `n(new Error("http status code: " + s))` files a sentence as a dependency and `closure.mjs` exits 1 on an id that never existed. **Membership** decides which ledger it lands in: `requires` stays closed over this map, which is exactly what the closure gate asserts, and `externalRequires` records the rest. Upstream v0.1.73 arrived at the same field from the other side and this fork keeps its name, but not its single predicate: upstream admits only a `./`-prefixed string, so a cross-chunk edge spelled as a content hash or an ordinal still disappears with no trace. Shape here is three spellings — hash, small ordinal, and a `./` path id — and the path spelling is gated **twice**, on the literal being a string token AND on the container keying its own modules by path, because in a numeric container `s(cond ? "./assets/logo.svg" : …)` is an asset URL and admitting it re-opens the false-dependency half of the same bug. ⭐ `closure.mjs` prints the outbound edges instead of failing on them (a chunk depending on another chunk is normal; it only matters once the slice ships standalone, where it throws at evaluation time from a byte-identical slice), and the set empties on its own once a site-wide map exists;
- enhances CLI ergonomy for `verify-mirror.mjs` (`--root` alias, default `external.txt` excuses) and `verify-offline.mjs` (`--url` single-URL shortcut);
- provides generic SPA interactive navigation and hydration gate templates (`assets/templates/verify-spa-navigation.mjs` and `navigation.config.example.mjs`) with continuous rAF animation pumping and opacity stability verification;
- extends `scripts/serve.mjs` text rewriting to extension-less files. The type is decided the way `mirror-site.mjs` already decides it (`isTextRefSource`): **the origin's declared type first** — `mirror-manifest.json` records it per entry and upstream v0.1.69 taught this server to read it — **and the bytes only for rows that carry none**, a mirror taken before the field existed or a response the origin sent bare. The sniff is `sniffTextBytes` **imported from `lib/extract-refs.mjs`**, the same predicate `verify-mirror` uses to decide which files to scan for references; a private copy here (the first version was one, stricter: fatal UTF-8 decode) disagrees on text that is not valid UTF-8, and the disagreement reads as the ledger claiming a reference is localised while the bytes going out still carry the absolute URL. ⚠ The first version of this asked the response's own `content-type`, which is computed as `MIME[ext] || "application/octet-stream"` and is therefore a **constant** for the one case it was consulted for; it answered "not text" every time and the branch never executed. **A check whose input is derived from its own condition is not a check**, and it failed silently — the files went out unrewritten exactly as before, and no gate looks at a mirrored API cache. ⚠ This branch and upstream's `RECORDED_TYPE` are complementary, not redundant: `localRelPath` stores an extension-less ORIGIN URL as `<path>/index.html`, so upstream's motivating case (a Nuxt server route) never reaches an `ext === ""` test at all, and the subject here is the CROSS-HOST files under `assets/<host>/`. Because the widening carries the rewrite into a class upstream never rewrites, it also re-keys upstream's v0.1.61 length-prefix guard from `ext === ".html"` onto the content itself (`hasFlight(text)`) and adds a `repairFlightRows` path for the bare, push-less RSC row stream. Left as upstream wrote it, the guard would miss exactly the documents it exists to protect: the failure it prevents shows zero 404s, zero request failures and an identical byte count;
- adds `?__probe&__noio` to `scripts/probe-shim.js`, leaving `IntersectionObserver` native while the rest of the determinism shim still applies, so a run can be compared against itself with and without the IO takeover.
- adds optional, configuration-driven coordinate and sourceification checks (`verify-ledger.mjs`, `verify-sourceified-tokens.mjs`) plus the Babel-based `demangle-modules.mjs` transformer. These operate on caller-provided records and ranges; they do not infer a site's structure or replace the existing stage gates.

### Upstream defect corrections

These are defects in upstream's own checks rather than differences of preference. They are listed apart from the additions above only because they would become redundant if upstream ever corrects them; until then this fork carries the corrections.

- **`lib/shell-build.mjs` / `serve.mjs` — the data-island guard landed on one of the two localisers.** v0.1.71 carves Nuxt's `__NUXT_DATA__` island out before localisation, because the app PARSES those entries and rewriting the deploy's own site record made a WebGL boot fail three layers away with every request still 200. The lesson is right; the placement is not. `verification-gates.md` §4.9.4 states that localisation exists TWICE here — this table at build time, `serve.mjs` at response time — and that whatever they must agree on lives in `lib/` and is imported by both. Measured against the merge commit's server, an island served through it comes back as `[{"url":"/","env":"live"},"/island.png"]`, which is exactly the rewrite the builder had just been taught not to do. Either the response layer undoes the guard, or the two sides disagree about one field and `verify-payload`'s classifier reads `https://host` against `/` as a content difference — reddening the payload gate on the target class the guard exists for. ⭐ The carve-out now lives in `lib/data-island.mjs` and both localisers import it, and it covers Nuxt 3's **externalized** payload too: §4.18 and §4.19 landed in one commit and were never connected, but `_payload.json` is the same devalue program input with the `<script>` wrapper off, and `.json` is in `serve.mjs`'s `TEXT_REWRITE`. ⚠ The carve-out is also a **trade**, and this fork makes it visible rather than asserting it away: a serialised payload is precisely where this toolchain measured latent outbound before (11 media-host URLs survived every other localisation shape; the runtime probe caught one), so "zero-outbound is unaffected" is a measurement of one site's island, not a property of islands. Preserved URLs are returned rather than swallowed — `build-site.mjs` fails on any that names a file, `serve.mjs` names each one once and keeps answering.

- **`verify-payload.mjs` — a 404 on the payload file kills the gate instead of failing it.** v0.1.71 taught the gate Nuxt 3's externalized `/_payload.json` and added two `await get(...)` calls outside any try, in a file where every await is top-level. Measured against a side that does not serve the file: a stack trace after route 1, route 2 never checked, no summary line — "the gate is broken" reported for "this side cannot produce its payload", the distinction `verify-offline.mjs` already states at its own head. ⚠ The path is also derived from side A and applied to side B **with side A's build id attached**, so a rebuild 404s for a file it serves under its own name (measured: A on `/_payload.json` against B on `/build-xyz/_payload.json` died; it passes now). Fetch failures become FAIL lines while anything that is not a fetch failure still throws, each side derives the path from its own document, and a shape disagreement between the sides is reported as the finding it is rather than surfacing as that same 404. ⚠ v0.1.73's `--allow-absent` is carried, rebuilt on this structure: upstream checks the other side with a bare `extract(html)`, which sees inline shapes only, so a side serving an **external** payload reads as "no island" and the run reports the two sides in agreement while one of them has a payload the other never had. Both sides go through the same `payloadOf` here; measured on a fixture, upstream's spelling passes that case and this one fails it.

- **`probe.mjs` — the flag enumeration omits two flags the file reads.** v0.1.70 added `KNOWN_FLAGS` so an unknown flag dies loudly instead of being silently ignored — the fix for a three-hour ghost hunt caused by passing `netcapture`'s `--settle` to `probe`. The set shipped without `expect-side` (read at L166) and `evalAfterDelay` (L421), so `probe.mjs <url> --expect-side mirror` — the cross-side assertion `scripts/README.md` documents — exits 2 with `FATAL: unknown flag(s)`. ⚠ A fix for a silent ignore that false-FATALs on its own arguments is the same defect one sign over: a hand-maintained second copy of a fact the code already states, drifting from it. Both names added, and the reconciliation left beside the set as one grep.

- **`cold-audit-modules.mjs` — the coverage gate did not run whenever the check found anything.** The 80% gate added in v0.1.50 was written as an `else if` after the suspicious-call-site branch, so any candidate skipped it entirely. Confirmed on a real chunk (lights, `module-map-b30f9f2`, 65 modules): upstream examined 48 of them — 73.8%, under its own threshold — printed four review candidates, and exited 0 PASS. The four candidates were themselves false positives (`n(new Error("http status code: " + f.statusCode))` and friends, a node-style callback that survives the arity and `new` heuristics), so the gate was not traded away for a finding but for noise. This is the third appearance of the failure mode v0.1.50 was written to close, and a gate hanging off an `else` branch is not a gate. Now evaluated unconditionally.

- **`cold-audit-modules.mjs` — the packer was inferred from the factory shape instead of the container.** v0.1.50 computed `TURBO` from `MAP.container` and then never used it, deciding instead that an arrow factory means Turbopack. Webpack 5 emits `(module, exports, require) => {}` on modern targets — Next.js output is literally `(e,t,r)=>{` — so the first parameter was taken for a Turbopack `ctx` and searched for `e.i(`, finding no requires while still counting toward coverage. The arrow branch also required a `^`, `,` or `[` prefix that the indented `id: (e, t, r) => {` head js-beautify produces never satisfies, so on a webpack 5 bundle every module fell through to 0% coverage instead. Now the container decides, webpack arrow factories resolve the third parameter, and factories with no require binding are counted and reported separately rather than deflating coverage. ⚠ v0.1.69 resolved the same dead binding the other way — it **deleted** `TURBO` and kept the shape guess — and v0.1.73 then rebuilt arrow support on top of that guess, keying the webpack arm on a `:` before the factory and counting parameter-less factories as plain `examined`. So this correction diverges from upstream by intent rather than by omission, in two places: a container-keyed rule needs no `:` anchor and survives an unquoted key, and "nothing to look at" is tallied apart from "looked and found nothing" — which is the distinction the coverage figure exists to report.

- **`verify-mirror.mjs` — `avif` and `mp4` were the same predicate.** Both were spelled as an ISO-BMFF `ftyp` box at offset 4, which is byte-identical in a still image and in a video, so the type-confusion check could not tell the two kinds apart at all. Harmless while every mismatch was a hard failure; not harmless under v0.1.73, which downgrades "declared `image/*`, bytes are another known image format" to an informational lead on the grounds that it is the origin's own labeling habit. With the overlap in place an **MP4 body sitting under an `image/jpeg` declaration** matches the image kind and is waved through as a labeling quirk — a substitution this gate exists to catch, excused by the mechanism added to excuse a different one. The decision now reads the brand list, major and compatible both (an AVIF still routinely ships `major=mif1`, and a video container can carry a HEIF-family brand, so the major brand alone leaves the overlap one layer down), and `mp4` is defined as the complement so the two are mutually exclusive by construction. The downgrade itself is carried unchanged.

- **`lib/urlpath.mjs` — the path-tail flatten is written twice and marks its output as a page.** v0.1.73 flattens a URL path that continues past a file (`…/team-hero.jpg/m/110x110/filters:…`) into one `@@`-joined filename, which is right — the alternative needs `team-hero.jpg` to be a file and a directory at once. Two problems in the shipped form. The regex is **copied** into `localRelPath` and `serveCandidates`, in the one module whose entire purpose is that the crawler, the server, the capture and the gates cannot each hold their own answer (§2.1.1); it is one exported `flattenPathTail` here. And the flattened tail rarely ends in an extension, so the page/asset test below it classified `…filters:format(avif):quality(70)` as a **page** and wrote `…/index.html`, while `serveCandidates` offered the flattened name without one — writer and server disagreeing on every transformed asset, which is the exact drift the flatten was added to remove. The flatten only fires on a known asset extension, so having fired is itself the evidence that the path names a file, and it is now treated as one.

- **`beautify-bundle.mjs` — the corruption fallback ships minified bytes as the coordinate system and exits 0.** v0.1.69 re-parses beautified output and, on failure, writes the ORIGINAL bytes to `_pretty/` — correct, because they are at least valid. But `_pretty/` exists to be the coordinate system every `file:line` citation resolves against, and for such a file there are no line numbers: the bundle is one line, `module-map` gives every module `startLine == endLine == 1`, and `cold-audit` then reads the entire file as each module's body at 100% coverage. The warning printed mid-run, hundreds of `npx` lines above the prompt, from a command that reported success. Now marked in the `_pretty/` ledger and FATAL at the end of the run, after the artefacts are written — the same shape as the injectivity assertion beside it.

- **`name-modules.mjs` — the Turbopack reader matches any `.push([…])`.** The `CallExpression` visitor added in v0.1.69 accepts any member call named `push` whose first argument is an array, then reads `(id, function)` pairs out of it — so a route table, a plugin registry or a `handlers.push([2, cb])` yields a "module factory" and the tool names a callback. `module-map.mjs` identifies the same container by requiring the literal `TURBOPACK` identifier. ⚠ **Two tools disagreeing about what the container is** is the same defect as two copies of a reference shape: whichever is looser decides, and nothing reports that they diverged. Anchored on `TURBOPACK` here too.

- **`verify-mirror.mjs` — the closure gate writes its own output into the mirror.** v0.1.69 dumps the complete gap list to `<mirror>/closure-gap.txt` (right: the console listing is truncated, and seeding from a truncated list converges on nothing) and then adds the filename to `LEDGER_FILES` so the coverage check ignores it. ⛔ `mirroring.md` §0 makes the mirror inviolable — it is both the reverse-engineering evidence and the comparison baseline — so a verification pass that MUTATES its own subject has spent that guarantee to save a path argument, and an exclusion is not a fix for an artefact that should not be there. Now `--gap-out`, defaulting outside the mirror; the ledger exemption stays for mirrors that already carry the file.

- **`netcapture.mjs` — `--fetch` wrote one ledger, and v0.1.69's second one is written inside a swallowing `try`.** Appending only the inventory row left every gap it closed failing `verify-mirror` twice — once as a coverage orphan, once as an inventory row absent from the manifest — and any later `mirror-site` run rewrites both ledgers from the manifest, silently dropping it again. v0.1.69 adds the manifest write but wraps it in `try { … } catch {}`, so a missing or half-written manifest skips the write with no message; it also stores the declared type as `.split(";")[0]`. ⚠ Stripping the parameters matters because `serve.mjs` now answers FROM this field: a mirrored `.html` row recorded as bare `text/html` overrides the `MIME[".html"]` default that carries `charset=utf-8`. This fork read-modify-writes the whole document (preserving `origin`, rebuilding a missing `files`) and stores the origin's declaration verbatim.

- **`pixel-walk.mjs` — `--rescroll-ms` could exceed the pump budget and disable itself in silence.** The re-issued scroll runs on virtual pump time, so once `--rescroll-ms` reaches `dt x frames` its `setTimeout` is never pumped. `--pump 16.7,60` alone is enough to kill the default `--rescroll-ms 1500`. Now a hard failure that names the frame count required. ⚠ Upstream v0.1.58 moved driving into the pump loop (`--drive`), which independently covers the walk-collapses-to-one-position failure this guard was originally written for, so the guard's stated rationale was rewritten rather than left to mislead: it stays because the combination silently drops a scroll the caller explicitly asked for, not because the walk would degrade.

- **`module-map.mjs` — the new module aliases were looked up by id, and ids repeat.** v0.1.54 attaches `aliases` to each module with `entries.find((e) => String(e.id) === String(id))`, but the same file documents that a container can define one id more than once (597 properties, 569 distinct modules, 4 shadowed definitions that are not byte-identical to their winner). The lookup returns the first definition, so an alias can be hung on a shadowed body and `slice-modules.mjs` will then emit that alias pointing at the wrong factory — surfacing as the same `the module factory is not available` the alias support exists to prevent, one level harder to trace. Now carried from the loop variable.

- **`module-map.mjs` / `pixelcompare.mjs` — dead binding and broken formatting carried in with v0.1.54 and v0.1.59.** The rewritten coverage gate kept a `reqCalls` counter that nothing reads once `reqCallIdx.length` replaced it; the landing-position gate landed with `}    } else {` and an unindented block inside `{ const { a, b } = ... }`. Neither changes behaviour; both are cleaned up.

- **`verify-refs-served.mjs` — the raw and decoded scans are unioned, and here a superset is a verdict.** The gate added in v0.1.68 scans each document twice (raw, and with entities and backslash escapes decoded) and adds both passes' captures to one set. That is right for a CLOSURE scan, where an extra spelling costs one redundant lookup; here every member of the set is asked of the server and reported as a missing asset when it 404s. The `/_next/image` branch decodes its own capture, so it is clean — the second branch did not, so the raw pass contributed `…?auto=format,compress&amp;w=700`, a spelling that in HTML means `&` and nothing else. Measured on artisansdidees: 44 rows reported missing, every file present on disk. That is the phantom-reference failure this toolchain has now met three times (push boundaries in v0.1.62, `${` template prefixes in v0.1.66), this time inside a gate written to close it. Now both branches decode their capture through the shared `decodeEntities` / `decodeUrlEscapes` rather than a local `replace(/&amp;/g, "&")`.

- **`probe-shim.js` — the `IntersectionObserver` takeover normalised semantics without an opt-out or a disclosure.** Intersection is computed against the viewport with `isIntersecting = ratio > 0`, discarding `root`, `rootMargin` and `threshold`. Since both sides run the same shim, a rebuild and a mirror that genuinely disagree on a threshold are flattened onto the same frame and pass. The takeover is kept — its measured benefit is real — but each observer now reports which options were discarded, and `&__noio` provides the control run. Also fixed: `disconnect()` left the record in the pump's walk list, holding element references and costing a forced layout per frame for every dead observer; and `deliverIntersections` walked the live array, so a one-shot reveal disconnecting from inside its own callback caused the next observer to be skipped for that frame.
